slides.texte_overlay:
Why every man should keep
a simple journal
It clears your head. Writing down what's on your mind before bed stops thoughts from spinning while you try to sleep.
It shows you patterns. After a month, you'll notice what drains you, what lifts you and what keeps repeating. Patterns become obvious.
It makes decisions easier. Writing the pros and cons on paper is calmer and clearer than going round in circles in your head.
It keeps your memories. Small funny moments, trips, conversations. In a few years, you'll love reading it back.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Write one thing you learned in your journal each night.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Write one thing you learned in your journal each night.

slides.texte_overlay: Keep it short. Three lines a day is enough. A simple habit you keep beats a perfect one you drop. Start tonight with three lines.
Nobody has to read it. Be honest. A journal is the one place where you don't have to impress anyone. Write freely.
